newsitem.title: CANADA: Immigration spurs Canada population growth.
newsitem.headline: Immigration spurs Canada population growth.

text.p: Boosted by immigration, Canada's population growth in 1995 was the highest in the Western industrialised world, the government statistics agency said on Tuesday.
Canada's population expanded by 1.3 percent in 1995, with more than half the gains coming from immigration, Statistics Canada said.
The growth was 4-1/2 times that of Europe and also topped growth rates in the United States and Australia.
Canada's population rose to an estimated 29.8 million at Jan. 1, 1996, from 29.4 million the year before.

The country's fertility rate was unchanged at 1.64 children per woman, while the abortion rate rose slightly to 487 per 1,000 women in 1994 -- the latest year for which statistics were available -- from 480 in 1993.
Life expectancy was unchanged at 75.1 years for men and 81.2 years for women.

Alzheimer's disease was a growing affliction in Canada, causing more deaths than AIDS in 1994, Statistics Canada said. Alzheimer's killed 1,685 women and 859 men in 1994, compared to 139 women and 1,489 men who died from AIDS.
Quebec's suicide rate was the highest in Canada in 1994, with the French-speaking province averaging 27.2 suicides for every 100,000 people. The suicide rate in Canada's nine other provinces fell.
